messages.subject: Error in bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

I have successfully set up the  new BioGeoBEARS from git hub.  I changed the manual dispersal multiplier values from 0 to a small value, revisited areas_adjacency, and specified the areas allowed matrix (manually). But I am unable to get rid of the following error .

Error in bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

STOP ERROR #3 in bears_optim_run(). Test calculation of the likelihood with calc_loglike_for_optim_stratified() returned LnL=NaN, which is not a valid starting likelihood. Probably, you have an overly constrained analysis and have thus made your data impossible. For example, if your tips had ranges A and B, but you disallowed the state AB, then your data would be impossible under DEC, because AB is a required intermediate state. Try removing some of the areas allowed/area adjacency/manual states list constraints.  You can also try changing manual dispersal multipliers from 0 to some small value (e.g. 0.00001) -- note that this can works on dispersal multiplers, but NOT on area constraints, which have to be 0 or 1.  Have a CAREFUL THINK about what you are doing and why you think the list of ranges should be so constrained - do you actually have a good argument for your constraints?

messages.subject: confused by event timing in BSM output
messages.subject_clean: confused by event timing in BSM output
messages.body_plain:
Hi BioGeoBEARS group,

I have been trying to develop rates for some transition events based on anagenetic events tables. I want to know the amount of time spent in areas being dispersed from along terminal branches that contain quite a few transition events within each simulation. Upon visual inspection I am confused. The events do not seem to naturally flow into one another on the same branch timing-wise. For example, I have two events occurring on the same terminal branch. The earliest event to occur on that branch (AB->ABC) occurred ~ 3.32 mya according to the abs_event_time column. The next most recent event (AB->ABC, again) occurred ~ 2.42 mya. Perhaps I’m missing something, using the wrong column to look at event time, or something worse, but shouldn’t the next event have started in range ABC? Any advice on how to obtain the segment length of branches spent in any particular area would be greatly appreciated!

My model is constrained to only allow transitions into adjacent areas.

best,
Chauncey Gadek
